newsitem.title: USA: Ice, snow slowing grain, livestock movement - trade.
newsitem.headline: Ice, snow slowing grain, livestock movement - trade.

text.p: Ice and snow across most of the Midwest was slowing the pace of livestock and grain movement to market early Monday, and more wintry weather was expected during the day, forecasters said.

"They've (the Midwest) had occasional snow on Friday and yesterday (Sunday) which has made for transportation problems throughout much of the Midwest," said Joel Burgio, forecaster with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.

Ice and blowing snow has slowed hog movement in Iowa and southern Minnesota, while ice and snow in Illinois, Ohio and Indiana has left roads treacherous and slowed grain transportation, cash dealers said.
Slick roads hampered movement of hogs to market in some areas and buoyed prices on supplies that were available, livestock dealers and packer sources said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department said hogs sold in Iowa/southern Minnesota at prices steady to $0.50 per cwt higher than top prices Friday, with an early top of $55.00.

The system that brought the wintry weather over the weekend was expected to gradually move eastward on Monday, but light to moderate snow was expected in more northern areas of the Midwest before the storm leaves the region, Burgio said.
Snowfall totals for Monday in the northern Midwest could be up to four inches before skies clear overnight, said Fred Gesser, forecaster with Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.
"Arctic air will move back in as the skies clear," Gesser said. "We'll see sub-zero lows across Nebraska and Iowa and single digits in Kansas."
Temperatures were expected to warm on Wednesday before another system moves into the Midwest Thursday, Gesser said.
"On Thursday we go back to Arctic air," Gesser said.
There is a chance for more snow or ice again on Friday and Saturday as a weather system moves into the Midwest from the western U.S., Gesser said.
